questions.text: A cuboid has dimensions (2x + 3), (3x – 1), and 5x. Find the total surface area of this cuboid, given that x = 4.
Two straight lines have equations: 3x – y = 5 and x + 3y = 15. They intersect at point R. Find the coordinates of point R using an algebraic method. Clearly show all steps.
questions.markingGuide: From eq 1: y = 3x – 5. Sub into eq 2: x + 3(3x – 5) = 15. x + 9x – 15 = 15. 10x = 30. x = 3. y = 3(3) – 5 = 4. R = (3, 4). Achieved = eliminate one variable. Merit = correct coordinates with algebraic method.

questions.text: Rectangle ABCD has width AB = 40 cm and length AD = 1.2 m. Point T lies on side BC. Angle ATB = 30°. Find the perimeter of triangle ATD.
questions.markingGuide: AD = 1.2 m = 120 cm. AB = 40 cm. In triangle ABT right-angled at B with angle ATB = 30°: tan(30°) = AB/BT → BT = 40/tan(30°) = 40/0.5774 = 69.28 cm. AT = AB/sin(30°) = 40/0.5 = 80 cm. BC = AD = 120 cm, so TC = 120 – 69.28 = 50.72 cm. TD = √(CD² + TC²) = √(40² + 50.72²) = √(1600 + 2572.5) = √4172.5 = 64.59 cm. Perimeter = AT + TD + AD = 80 + 64.59 + 120 = 264.59 cm ≈ 264.6 cm. Achieved = finding one side length. Merit = correct perimeter with working.

questions.text:
The table below shows the relationship between x and y values in a sequence.

Find an equation that represents y for any given x-value. Show your working.
questions.markingGuide: Subtract 2 from each y: 6, 18, 54, 162, 486. These are 6, 18, 54, 162, 486 — each multiplied by 3. This is 6 × 3^(x-1) = 2 × 3^x. So y = 2 × 3^x + 2. Check: x=1: 6+2=8 ✓, x=2: 18+2=20 ✓, x=3: 54+2=56 ✓. Achieved = identifies base 3 multiplier. Excellence = fully correct equation with working.

questions.text: The graph of y could be drawn for all values of x. Identify THREE different features of the graph of y, using your equation found in part (d)(i).
questions.expectedAnswer: E.g. exponential shape, y-intercept at (0, 4), horizontal asymptote at y = 2
questions.markingGuide: Using y = 2×3^x + 2: (1) y-intercept at (0, 2×1+2) = (0, 4). (2) Horizontal asymptote at y = 2 as x → –∞. (3) Exponential growth as x → +∞. (4) No x-intercepts (always > 2). (5) Always increasing. Achieved = one feature. Merit = two features. Excellence = at least three features with justification.

questions.text: Triangle PQR has angle P = 3x, angle Q = (2x + 10)°, and angle R = (x + 20)°. Find the value of x.
questions.markingGuide: Angles sum to 180°: 3x + (2x + 10) + (x + 20) = 180. 6x + 30 = 180. 6x = 150. x = 25. Award Achieved for x = 25.

questions.text: Triangle EFG lies flat with a right angle at E. Point H is directly above E (vertical line HE). HF = 12 cm. Angle HFE = 25°, angle EFG = 55°. Find the size of angle HGE.
questions.markingGuide: In triangle HEF (right-angled at E): HE = 12 × sin 25° = 5.071 cm; EF = 12 × cos 25° = 10.876 cm. In triangle EFG (right-angled at E, angle EFG = 55°): EG = EF × tan 55° = 10.876 × 1.4281 = 15.531 cm. In triangle HEG (right-angled at E): tan(angle HGE) = HE/EG = 5.071/15.531 = 0.3265. Angle HGE = 18.08° ≈ 18.1°. Achieved = finding HE or EF. Excellence = correct angle with full working.

questions.text: Factorise AND solve the equation: 12x² = 1 + x. Give your answer(s) as simplified fractions.
questions.markingGuide: 12x² – x – 1 = 0. Factorise: (3x – 1)(4x + 1) = 0. x = 1/3 or x = –1/4. Achieved = correct rearrangement. Merit = correct factorisation AND both solutions.

questions.text:
A pool is dug in the ground. The top section is rectangular: 15 m wide and 10 m deep. Below this, the pool widens symmetrically by 15 m on each side, making the bottom 45 m wide and 5 m deep. The pool is 40 m long.

1 m³ of earth weighs 800 kg. One truck can carry 25 tonnes per load.

Calculate the number of truck trips required to remove all the earth. Show full working.
questions.markingGuide: Top section: 15 × 10 × 40 = 6000 m³. Bottom section is trapezoidal: area = ½(15 + 45) × 5 = 150 m². Volume = 150 × 40 = 6000 m³. Total = 12000 m³. Weight = 12000 × 800 = 9,600,000 kg = 9600 tonnes. Trips = 9600/25 = 384 trips. Achieved = one volume correct. Merit = total volume correct. Excellence = correct trips with rounding justified.

questions.text: A straight line passes through points (–2, 7) and (6, 3). Find the equation of this line.
A parabola has vertex at (2, 9) and passes through (–1, 0) and (5, 0). Find its equation. Justify your working.
questions.markingGuide: Using vertex form: y = a(x – 2)² + 9. Substitute (5, 0): 0 = a(9) + 9. a = –1. So y = –(x – 2)² + 9. Or using intercept form: y = a(x + 1)(x – 5). Substitute (2, 9): 9 = a(3)(–3) = –9a. a = –1. Achieved: equation with incorrect a-value. Merit: correct equation with justification.

questions.text: A quarter of a circle has radius p and centre C at the bottom-left corner. The arc runs from point A (directly above C) to point B (directly right of C). Calculate how much longer the arc AB is than the straight line AB. Give your answer in terms of p.
questions.markingGuide: AB (straight line) = √(p² + p²) = p√2. Arc AB = (1/4)(2πp) = πp/2. Difference = πp/2 – p√2 = p(π/2 – √2). Achieved = correct AB or arc length. Merit = correct difference with working.

questions.text: A right-angled triangle has two short sides x/3 cm and 2x cm. The area of the triangle is 48 cm². Find the value of x.
questions.markingGuide: Area = ½ × (x/3) × 2x = x²/3 = 48. x² = 144. x = 12 (taking positive root). Achieved = correct area formula setup. Excellence = x = 12 with full working.
